analysis:
The PR changes first-token deadline admission in the provider's local engine bridge (EngineV2Bridge*.swift). It adds three things: a decode-step shape EWMA (engineDecodeShape, Measurements.swift:111-125), an isolated-prefill admission rate resolver anchored on the calibration-cell rate (Admission.swift:98-106; RateObservations.swift:55), and a coversObservation-based reset for late samples (RateObservations.swift:33-40). These are gated by the admissionFixes flag, which is resolved once per bridge (EngineV2Bridge.swift:393-399). The affected area is local scheduling and availability, specifically T-010/T-029-style resource use. It involves no coordinator protocol, key material, attestation, encryption or prefix-cache storage.

Confidentiality and integrity: no prompt content, plaintext, or cache scope or salt handling is touched. The TTL, HMAC lookup and SSD paths relevant to T-041 are unchanged. The changed files appear in T-041's affected_files list only because of the bridge, and the visible hunks touch no cache logic. The unchanged pre-submit retirement and release code (Admission.swift:135-309) was read and holds no new regressions.

Numeric safety: the decode shape divides by decodeSteps only after checking decodeSteps > 0. Each value is clamped to the range 1..64 and non-finite values are mapped to 1. engineDecodeRate already bounds tps to at most 20000.

Availability angle: IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate.resolve and DeadlineAdmissionFixes.decodeRateShape are defined outside the supplied evidence. Whether they could over-admit work, under-admit work, or reject all traffic cannot be established from this evidence. Admission is also not a security boundary against the provider's own operator; it governs only the provider's own capacity.

Open question for the next pass: the unseen implementations (the resolver, coversObservation, updateDecodeTpsEwma with a shape argument, and the engine-side CBv2DecodeRateShape handling) should be checked for fail-safe behaviour with an uninitialised or stale anchor.
